chapters.title: Why it really ended (your side of it)
chapters.teaser: Not who was right. What your soul was doing while it fell apart.

chapters.title: Your breakup pattern
chapters.teaser: How you end things, how you grieve, and the habit that slows you down.

chapters.title: Why you keep checking
chapters.teaser: What the pull back toward them is really asking for.

chapters.title: So, will they come back? The honest answer
chapters.teaser: What a chart can and can't tell you, and the question that matters more.

chapters.title: If they ever reach out
chapters.teaser: Three questions to ask before you reply, built for your soul.

chapters.title: What you do now
chapters.teaser: The next small steps that help, whatever they decide.

text.why-it-ended: Mu Earth is the mountain: steady, protective, impossible to push around. You were probably the solid one in that relationship, the person who showed up and held everything together. Mountains are wonderful to lean on. They're also hard to move. If your partner wanted change, spontaneity or more open emotion, they may have felt like they were knocking on rock. Or you carried too much for too long without ever saying how heavy it was, until the ground cracked. Either way, look at the moments you chose stillness when something in you already knew a conversation was needed.
text.your-breakup-pattern: You don't break, you erode. Mu Earth endures a lot quietly and gives a relationship every possible chance. Then, once you've decided, you rarely come back. After a breakup you keep the schedule, go to work, look completely fine. People may assume it didn't hurt. It did. It just went inward, into the bedrock. Your pattern is staying functional and skipping the feeling, which works for a while and then shows up as tiredness, or sudden irritation at people who did nothing wrong. Let yourself be visibly sad with someone you trust. A mountain is allowed to have weather.
text.the-pull: What pulls you back is loyalty and habit. You built something with them, routines, favourite places, maybe a whole circle of shared friends, and you hate leaving a structure half finished. You might also feel responsible for them and wonder whether they're okay. That's your protective side. But being someone's mountain doesn't mean you owe them permanent shelter. Notice whether you miss them, or the shape your life used to have. Shapes can be rebuilt. Start small: a new Saturday ritual, a different way home, a dinner you cook only for yourself.
text.the-honest-answer: Another person's choices are not in your chart. Nobody can honestly tell you whether they'll come back, so we won't. What we can look at is the mountain. Mu Earth tends to wait, solid and patient, for the other person to move first. If you're waiting now, ask what exactly you're waiting for. If it ended because you were hard to reach, any reunion would need you to open up in ways you didn't before. If it ended because you carried everything, it would need them to carry more. Either way, the work starts with you saying out loud what you need.
text.if-they-reach-out: If they reach out, you'll probably answer calmly and politely and reveal almost nothing. That protects you, but it tells neither of you anything. Decide first what you want: friendship, a real second try, or simply peace. Then say it plainly. Mu Earth is brilliant at stability and terrible at saying I was hurt. Try saying it anyway. If you do reconnect, set a slow pace with clear conversations, not a quiet slide back into old routines. And if your gut says no, that's a complete answer. Mountains don't have to explain why they stayed where they were.
text.what-you-do-now: Shift your ground a little. Mu Earth heals through movement it chooses for itself. Rearrange a room. Hike somewhere new. Take a weekend away alone. Let one trusted friend see that you're not fine, just for an evening. Point your protective energy at yourself for once: rest, decent food, fewer obligations for a while. Then try one thing with no plan at all, a last-minute invite, a spontaneous yes. Not because you need to change who you are. Because a mountain that feels a little wind is still a mountain. Just one that's wide awake.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You held everything together, Mu. That took real strength.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It also took zero sentences about how you felt. Rocks can talk.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Missing your old routine is normal. It was home.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Rebuild the routine. Don't rebuild them into it by default.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Let one friend see that you're sad. Just one.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Their choices aren't yours to carry. Put the boulder down.

spring.intro: Spring is when roots break open the mountain. Wood ruled your birth season, Mu, and Wood controls Earth, so you were born under steady pressure to hold firm while things grew all over you. That made you dependable and very patient. In the relationship you were probably the solid one, absorbing their changes and moods without moving. When it ended, you might be confused because you didn't do anything wrong, and that's partly the point. Spring mountains forget they're allowed to move. Some of what pushed through you was growth, some was damage, and you let both in quietly. The honest question isn't whether they come back. It's what you'd stop absorbing if they did.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You absorbed everything and called it being steady. Mountains get cracks too.

summer.intro: A summer mountain is warm right through. Fire ruled your season, Mu, and Fire generates Earth, so your chart is well supported: confident, generous, hard to knock over. That's a real gift in a breakup. You will be okay, probably faster than you expect. The blind spot of sunlit Earth is certainty. You knew what the relationship was, you knew what you were offering, and it may have been hard for them to change anything about it. Mountains don't negotiate. If you're replaying the end, look for the moments they asked you to move and you stayed put out of habit. That's not blame. It's the part you can actually work with.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They asked you to budge. You were a mountain about it. Literally.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain gives up its ore. Metal ruled your season, Mu, and Earth generates Metal, so your energy pours out as results: practical help, steady action, things done. In love you probably showed up with deeds more than words. The breakup may have left you puzzled. You did so much, so why wasn't it enough? Sometimes the other person wanted the words, the feelings, the slow talk that deeds can't replace. Autumn Earth also tires quietly, because it gives without noticing it's being mined. If you feel hollow rather than heartbroken, that's why. Refill before you decide anything. Fire helps: warmth, rest, people who look after you for once.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You did so much for them, Mu. Let someone do something for you.

winter.intro: A winter mountain holds back a frozen river. Water ruled your birth season, Mu, and Earth controls Water, so you were born to be the dam: steady, containing, keeping big feelings in their banks. In the relationship you probably managed a lot, maybe their emotions as well as yours. After the breakup, the dam held. You look calm. Inside there's more water pressing than anyone knows. The pull back for winter Mu is responsibility: wondering whether they're okay, whether you should check in, whether you held it together well enough. Let some of the river through. Cry, talk, write it out. A dam that never releases isn't strong. It's just very full.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Checking if they're okay is still checking. Ask if you're okay.

strength.strong: Your mountain stands on solid ground, Mu. Plenty of Earth and Fire in your chart make you steady, protective and very hard to move. In love, that reliability is gold. In a breakup, it can be a wall. You may have held your position in every argument, sure that consistency was the same as care. The blind spot is that immovable can feel like unreachable. Your ex may have stopped trying to shift you. If you're replaying it, look for where a little give would have helped. Moving one stone doesn't topple a mountain.
strength.weak: With thin support around your Day Master, Mu, you became solid by force of will. In love you probably held everything together, even when nobody was holding you. You took on their stress, kept the peace, kept showing up. When it ended, you may feel like the ground shifted and you didn't see it coming because you were too busy carrying. That's not a failure of strength. It's a mountain built on borrowed soil. Let others carry something for you now. Steadiness should come with support, not instead of it.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and answers, even in heartbreak. You want a plan for getting over it, maybe even a plan for getting them back. Slow down. Not everything grows on schedule, and some things need to just sit for a while. Ask for help instead of turning healing into a project. For balance, let a little Metal in: declutter, finish old things, clear out the drafts folder. A clean edge helps Wood stop reaching for what's already gone.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means fresh starts feel heavy. After a breakup you might stay in the same place, emotionally and literally, for longer than you'd like. That isn't weakness. It just means new growth needs a nudge. Small steps work best: a new route to work, one new class, one new person a week. Get outside in the mornings and keep something green near you. You don't need a whole new life. You need one new branch, and then another.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes you feel everything at full volume. A breakup can feel like an emergency, with urges to text, post, or fix it all tonight. Your passion is real, but heat isn't a strategy. Before any big move, sleep on it. Cool down with water: swimming, long showers, quiet evenings at home. Talk to your calmest friend before your most exciting one. Let the fire warm you instead of burning through your peace.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means joy and visibility don't come easily, and after a breakup you might go dim for a while, hiding from people and from fun. Turn the lights back on gently. Sunshine, music, dancing in the kitchen, one social plan a week even when you'd rather stay in. Letting people see you is the medicine here. Warmth doesn't only live in romance. It's in friends, in laughter, in simply being out in the world.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you hold on: to routines, to memories, to the hope that things will settle back into their old place. Stability is your gift, but in heartbreak it can turn into staying stuck. Shake the ground a little. Move the furniture, take a short trip, try something unplanned. Let some Wood energy in, growth and new beginnings. You can keep what was good and still leave room for something new to grow.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means life can feel unsteady, and a breakup can knock away what little ground you had. You might feel scattered, unsure where to put your feet. Build structure gently: regular meals, a steady bedtime, one place at home that's only yours. Cook something. Walk somewhere. Lean on the people who are reliable. Stability first, big decisions later. You need solid ground under you before deciding anything about the past.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal makes you sharp and decisive, sometimes too quickly. You may have cut the relationship off cleanly and then refused to look at what you feel. Or you judge yourself harshly for every mistake you made in it. Soften the edges. Let Water in: rest, tears, music, journaling. Feeling the grief isn't the same as reopening the door. You can keep your boundaries firm and still let your heart thaw.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard, so after a breakup you might keep the door half open, answer every message, or stay friends when it hurts. Practise clean edges. Mute without guilt. Box up their things. Say no without explaining. White and silver, tidy spaces and finished tasks all help your chart. A boundary isn't cold. It's how you protect the part of you that's still healing.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means you think and feel deeply, maybe endlessly. After a breakup you might drift through memories, analyse every detail, and lose sleep to what-ifs. Your intuition is a gift, but it needs riverbanks. Add some Earth: routines, cooking, walks, people who ground you. Give overthinking a time limit. Feel it fully, then get up and do one ordinary thing.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means rest and reflection get skipped. You may rush past the breakup, staying busy so you never have to sit with it. That works until suddenly it doesn't. Build in quiet on purpose: slow mornings, water by your bed, a few lines in a journal at night, a bath instead of another plan. Let yourself feel without fixing. Intuition grows when you give it some silence.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: So much Wood. You've drafted three versions of 'hey, random but' already.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy wants a goal. Give it your own plans, not their inbox.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: every feeling is a five-alarm emergency. It's a breakup, not an inferno.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is beautiful. Let it cool before you hit send on anything.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth. You'd still be in that relationship purely out of habit.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Just make sure you're loyal to yourself too.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. You cut them off cleanly, then reread everything at midnight.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Being firm protected you. Being gentle with yourself will heal you.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've cried to three songs and written a novel in your notes app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Feeling deeply is a gift. Just come up for air sometimes.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make moving on feel stuck. Small new routines count as growth.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: You haven't changed anything since the breakup, including your lock screen. Start there.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make joy feel far away. Borrow some from a loud friend.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: You stopped having fun when they left. Fun was never theirs to take.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth can make everything feel unsteady. Simple routines will hold you.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no anchor. You re-decide whether to text them every hour.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal makes boundaries tricky. You're allowed to say no to your own phone.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means you'll answer at 2am. Put the phone in another room.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make grief hide. It's okay to let it surface slowly.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: You said you're fine twelve times today. Water would like a word.

gap-wood.title: The tree that tried to move a mountain
gap-wood.text: You were with someone who arrived with a five-year plan and a list of ways you could be slightly better. Your Gap Wood ex meant well. They genuinely believed in you, which is why they kept suggesting the new job, the gym schedule, the earlier alarm. But every suggestion landed as 'you're not quite enough yet', and you did what mountains do: you went still. You didn't argue. You just stopped moving, and they read that as not caring, so they pushed harder, and you got quieter. Their texts arrived with times and plans; yours came hours later, short and honest. You felt hurried. They felt ignored. Nobody was lying. The ache is that you were loved and pressured in the same breath, and it's hard to grieve something like that cleanly. You miss their energy. They made life move, and on your own the days can sit very still. So choose one change you actually want, small and yours, and start it this week. Not to prove anything to them. To feel what growing is like when nobody is pushing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, your stillness isn't coldness. Some people just never learned to read it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, the mountain didn't need a coach. It needed company.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Growth and steadiness can share a landscape. Just not by force.

eul-wood.title: The vine that couldn't move the mountain
eul-wood.text: You were with someone who wanted to rearrange the furniture of your life, gently, with charm. Your Eul Wood ex texted often and playfully, with stickers and links and little jokes, and you replied when you could, short and honest. To you that was love. To them, your 'ok' read like a shrug. They found ways around you: a hint here, a suggestion dressed as a joke, a plan half made before you'd agreed. You noticed. You always notice. And noticing made you plant your feet. You found them inconsistent and busy; they found you slow, maybe even boring, which stung more than you let on. You were steady and it didn't count as romance, and that's the bruise. Here's something kind and true: steadiness is romance, but it needs translating. You miss their lightness. They made heavy days less heavy. So send something small and unnecessary to someone you love this week. A heart emoji. A photo of a dog. It costs a mountain almost nothing, and it says 'I'm here' in a language vines speak fluently.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, a single heart emoji would have changed so many evenings.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, their 'ok' was warm. It just wasn't decorated.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Charm doesn't move mountains. Honest asks sometimes do.

byeong-fire.title: Sunlight on a mountain that stayed home
byeong-fire.text: You loved the sun, and the sun wanted to go out every night. Your Byeong Fire ex was bright, impulsive, adored by everyone, and for a while their warmth made your quiet life glow. They texted twelve times; you answered once, carefully, completely. They made plans; you made dinner. When they wanted change, you didn't move, not because you didn't care but because moving is expensive for a mountain. In arguments they blazed. You went still and waited for the heat to pass, which they took as stonewalling, which made them louder. Being called boring by someone you were quietly devoted to is the part that still smarts. It wasn't boring. It was steady, and steadiness is hard to see in full daylight. You miss the light. Life with them had colour, and your evenings feel very grey now. Send a quick 'haha' sometimes, to anyone you love. Tiny responses tell energetic people you're still there. And try one new thing this month that you didn't plan. See how it feels to be warmed on purpose.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, a quick 'haha' costs nothing. Use it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, their one sentence meant more than your twelve. Count better.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sun and mountain. Gorgeous view. Terrible at arguments.

jeong-fire.title: A lantern in the mountain temple
jeong-fire.text: You were the mountain and they were the lantern, and it was a warm, quiet kind of good. Your Jeong Fire ex sent long, heartfelt messages; you replied with one honest line, every time. You thought that was enough, because to you showing up is the whole point. They wanted feelings spelled out. When something bothered them, they flickered quietly, and you didn't notice until it became a whole evening, and then you were baffled, because nothing had changed on your side. That bafflement felt to them like you didn't care. You did. You just experience love as presence, not commentary. Being told you were distant while you were standing right there is what stays with you. Their warmth is the pull. They lit up quiet places in you. Add one feeling word per message, starting now, with anyone. 'Home soon, missed you.' 'Good luck, proud of you.' It will feel unnecessary. It isn't. For some people, the word is the proof.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'it's fine' is not an emotional update.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, they always showed up. That was their love letter.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One feeling word per text. Not a speech. One word.

mu-earth.title: Two mountains, nobody moved
mu-earth.text: Two Mu Earths, side by side. Solid, safe, completely still. You didn't play games. 'Home at 7.' 'Ok.' Weekends had a rhythm, money was handled, the bins went out on the right night. Everything worked. The trouble was that nothing moved. When you disagreed, neither of you shifted, sometimes for days, and the longest argument in your flat may have been about a sofa. When something hurt, both of you said 'it's fine' and sat with it alone. Routine slowly became a rut, and boredom settled like fog on a ridge, and neither of you wanted to be the one to suggest change, because suggesting change feels like admitting something is wrong. There was no betrayal and no explosion. There was just a quiet ending that felt almost geological. The safety is what pulls you. With them, life was predictable in a way that let you rest. Practise starting change. Something small and slightly uncomfortable. A new restaurant, a class, a sentence that begins 'I've been feeling'. Send a friend something unnecessary today, just to feel what the first move is like. Mountains don't move often. When they do, the whole landscape changes.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'It's fine.' 'It's fine.' Two mountains, zero information.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You built something steady. That matters, even now.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Someone has to suggest the change. Practise being that someone.

gi-earth.title: Mountain and valley
gi-earth.text: Your Gi Earth ex was the valley next to your mountain: same landscape, very different mood. They worried. You said 'don't worry', which did not help. They asked caring questions; you replied with short, solid answers and didn't ask anything back. They did a lot of invisible work, the reminders, the shopping list, remembering your cousin's birthday, and you probably didn't notice much of it until it stopped. Both of you avoid conflict, so issues piled up quietly, like post you keep meaning to open. And then one day they said 'I'm tired', and you were genuinely surprised, because from your side everything had been fine. You were steady and loyal, and it turns out steady isn't the same as attentive. That lands hard. What you miss is how smoothly life ran with them in it. Ask one question back, every time. 'How was yours?' 'What's on your mind?' And look for the invisible work around you now. Notice it out loud. Being seen is the thing worriers need most.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you did so much quietly. Next time, say it out loud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'don't worry' has never once stopped a worrier from worrying.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Same landscape. Learn each other's weather.

gyeong-metal.title: The mountain holds the ore
gyeong-metal.text: Strength protecting strength: that was you and your Gyeong Metal ex. You were the mountain, they were the ore inside, and for a while it felt like a fortress. Both of you are proud. Both of you prefer action to talk. Your messages were short and efficient on both sides. The trouble was speed. They wanted change now; you wanted to think about it, maybe for a few months. Their impatience pushed at your slowness, and their bluntness bruised you in ways you didn't show, because you don't show hurt easily. Apologies were rare. Arguments were short but heavy, and afterwards there was a silence that felt like two walls facing each other. Neither of you said 'I'm hurt', because both of you would rather carry a mountain than admit to a bruise. Their honesty is what you miss. They were the one person you trusted to tell you the truth. Say one personal thing a day to someone close. Not logistics. 'I liked that.' 'I missed you today.' It isn't weakness. It's what keeps strong things from going cold.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, pushing a mountain is just tiring yourself out.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, they couldn't see your bruise. You have to show it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Strong and stronger. Neither said sorry. Classic.

sin-metal.title: The mountain guarding the gem
sin-metal.text: You were the mountain guarding the gem, and that felt like a role you were born for. Your Sin Metal ex was refined, sensitive, beautiful in a precise way, and you loved protecting that. But they also wanted to be appreciated out loud, specifically, often, and you're not a specific person. You show love by staying. They crafted messages carefully and waited for a thoughtful reply; you sent a short one. They hinted for weeks that something mattered, and you didn't catch it, and then they were hurt and you didn't know why. Their critiques of your simplicity stung more than you showed. Your slow emotional responses left them feeling unappreciated. You were guarding something you didn't fully understand, and that's a lonely way to love. What tugs is the preciousness. Being trusted by someone that delicate made you feel important. Compliment specifically. Not 'you look nice' but 'that colour makes your eyes look amazing'. It will feel like learning a new language. For jewels, it's the only one they really hear.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, their short reply still meant 'I'm here.' Mountains are like that.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'nice' is not a compliment. Be specific or be silent.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Steady love for a precious thing. It was real.

im-water.title: The dam and the river
im-water.text: You tried to contain the ocean, which, to be fair, is what earth does. Your Im Water ex was restless, brilliant, impossible to plan around. Plans changed by noon. Money came and went. You wanted routine; they found routine suffocating. You tried to build a dam, gently, with budgets and schedules and a calendar on the fridge. They pushed back. You dug in. They flooded. Every time you held tighter, the water pressed harder, until either the dam broke or the river found another way out. Their texts came in bursts and then silence; yours were steady and brief. Neither of you wanted to compromise. You weren't wrong to want stability, and they weren't wrong to want freedom, and it still couldn't work. That's what makes it hard to file away. Their aliveness is what you miss. Life with them had a motion you don't generate on your own. Allow irregularity somewhere. Leave one weekend unplanned. See how it feels to let something flow past you without catching it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, the calendar on the fridge was not romantic. To them, anyway.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, a steady text once a day doesn't make you a still pond.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Control versus flow. Nobody wins that. You both just get tired.

gye-water.title: Mist on the mountain
gye-water.text: A Heavenly Combination: mist on the mountain. Your Gye Water ex softened your edges, and you gave their drifting heart somewhere to rest. It was beautiful. It also kept running into the same wall: feelings versus facts. They shared feelings, poetic, emotional, half-formed. You replied practically. 'Have you tried sleeping earlier?' They didn't want a solution; they wanted to be met. Their moods confused you. Your steadiness, which you offered as love, sometimes felt to them like emotional absence. And your instinct to manage things made them feel contained. The worst evenings were the ones where you fixed and fixed and they went quieter and quieter. You were trying so hard to be helpful, and help wasn't what was being asked for. The softness is what pulls you back. Nobody else made your solid life feel so dreamy. Respond to the feeling before the fact. 'That sounds so heavy' before 'have you tried'. One sentence of simply being with someone. It's the hardest thing for a mountain and also the most powerful.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, 'have you eaten' was their way of saying 'I love you.'

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, not every sad message needs a five-step plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mist and mountain. Rare and beautiful. Learn the language.
